tasks.detail:
SENT BY THE CENTRAL ESTATE SURVEY on 2026-10-16, not raised by this project.

INFORMATION, NOT A FIX. The operator has agreed the rules below. New projects receive them in their CLAUDE.md from now on. This project is NOT bound by it at once: check this project against them and add your own tasks on your own schedule. Nothing in this project was changed except the appending of this task.

RULE 1 — SIGN-IN COMES FROM CENTRAL ACCESS:
  If this app has or needs a sign-in, do not build one: no user pool of its own, no shared or basic-auth password, no allow-list in code. Ask the operator to bring the app into central access. The join package arrives as a pull request in this repository, with its own guide and its two skills `/access-integrate` and `/access-maintain`; follow those. An app that already has its own login keeps it until the operator schedules the join; do not migrate it yourself.

RULE 2 — NO CREDENTIAL IN SERVED OR PUBLISHED CODE:
  No credential in any file a browser can fetch or that gets published: `public/`, static or docs site output, client bundles, committed docs or notes. This covers AWS keys, API keys (Anthropic included), tokens, passwords, and connection strings that contain passwords. Browser code gets no AWS credentials; it calls a backend or uses the app's sign-in. Backends and scripts read AWS credentials from the default credential chain (the runtime's role, or a profile chosen outside the code), never from literals or env files in the repository. A project never creates, copies or rotates an API key; it asks the operator. If you find a credential in tracked or served files, stop and tell the operator at once. Rotation comes first: deleting the value alone fixes nothing, because it stays in git history and on the live site.

WHAT TO CHECK: any sign-in this project builds itself (its own user pool, a shared or basic-auth password, an allow-list in code); any credential in public/, static or docs site output, client bundles, committed docs or notes; AWS credentials in browser code; AWS keys in literals or committed env files; an API key the project created or copied.

VERIFY, do not assume. The central repo has not read this project's files for this rule. If nothing above occurs here, that is an answer: record it and close this task. If the rule does not apply to this project at all, mark this task superseded with the reason.

tasks.detail:
SENT BY THE CENTRAL ESTATE SURVEY on 2026-10-19, not raised by this project. Its text was corrected in place on 2026-10-21: the rule now states its scope (the operator's internal apps).

INFORMATION, NOT A FIX. Nothing in this project was changed except the appending of this task.

The sign-in rule has changed. This notice supersedes the sign-in part of access-rules-2026-10; its rule on credentials in served or published code stands unchanged. Scope first: the rule is for the operator's internal apps (development tools, dashboards, project-management and operations pages, apps whose users are the operator's own people). A customer-facing product with its own user ecosystem (its own customer accounts, mobile apps, Sign in with Apple or other providers) keeps and builds the sign-in it needs, and nothing here migrates it. An app without a login needs nothing from this rule until it gets one. If an app with a login, or about to get one, is not clearly one kind or the other, ask the operator once and record the answer next to the rule in your CLAUDE.md. For an internal app with a login, the standard is now Google and an emailed code on the app's own sign-in page ("Continue with Google" and an email field), with no password form, no user pool of its own, no shared or basic-auth password and no allow-list in code. To ask for a join, send the onboarding-request form (app name and proposed id; who uses it; repo and production branch; AWS account and Region; framework and rendering; pages and roles; who should sign in; sender domain; what guards the app today; this session's name) to the operator in one line, or, when the central access session has already messaged this one, as a reply to it. Once a join is scheduled: register the owner-side tasks you receive through /add-work; these join steps, up to removing the old guard on central's go, need no further word from the operator; merge the delivery pull request with a merge commit; record the delivered files as not hand-editable; follow the delivered guide and skills; keep the old guard until central's go; show no support address; put any demo mode before the session check, guarded by a test. Never record a listed address in tracked files. An internal app with its own login keeps it, and nothing else changes, until the operator schedules its join. Plan your own compliance step by step, starting with putting the rule 'Sign-in Comes From Central Access' from the playbook's current CLAUDE.md template into your CLAUDE.md: replace yours if you have it, keeping its number, or add it as your next Critical Rule if you do not. For a customer-facing product, or an app without a login, that is all: the rule's scope exempts it.

RULE — Sign-in Comes From Central Access Agreed 2026-10-19; scope added 2026-10-21. Scope. This rule is for the operator's internal apps: development tools, dashboards, project-management and operations pages, apps whose users are the operator's own people. It does not apply to customer-facing products with their own user ecosystem (their own customer accounts, mobile apps, Sign in with Apple or other providers): those keep and build the sign-in they need, and nothing here migrates them. An app without a login needs nothing from this rule until it gets one. If an app with a login, or about to get one, is not clearly one kind or the other, ask the operator once and record the answer next to this rule. Every internal app with a login signs in the same way: Google and an emailed code, on the app's own sign-in page ("Continue with Google" and an email field). Do not build anything else: no password form, no user pool of its own, no shared or basic-auth password, no allow-list in code. - To join, send the onboarding request to the operator in one line, or, when the central access session has already messaged this one, as a reply to it. Fields: app name and proposed app id; who uses it (the operator's own people); repo and the branch that deploys production; AWS account and Region; framework and rendering (single-page or server-rendered); pages and the roles each needs; who should sign in (or "the operator decides"); sender domain wanted (or "the default"); what guards the app today; this session's name. - Register the owner-side tasks you receive through /add-work. Once the operator has scheduled the join (the owner-side tasks arrive from the central access session), these need no further word from the operator in this project: registering those tasks, merging the delivery pull request, integrating and deploying behind the old guard, the proof, and removing the old guard on central's go. Everything else follows this project's own checkpoints. The join package arrives as a pull request in this repository: merge it with a merge commit, record vendor/hyl-access-kit/, docs/central-access/ and .claude/skills/access-* as delivered and not hand-editable, and follow its guide and the skills /access-integrate and /access-maintain. - Defaults, not questions: no support address; demo mode, if the app has one, comes before the session check and is guarded by a test that production never sets it. - Keep the old guard until central access sends its go. Never record a listed address in tracked files. - An internal app that already has its own login keeps it until the operator schedules the join; do not migrate it yourself.

VERIFY, do not assume. The central repo has not read this project's files for this rule. If this project has no login, or is a customer-facing product with its own user ecosystem, that is an answer: record it and close this task.

tasks.detail:
SENT BY THE CENTRAL ESTATE SURVEY on 2026-10-12, not raised by this project.

INFORMATION, NOT A FIX. The operator has set a rule for VPN and SSH. New projects receive it in their CLAUDE.md from now on. This project is NOT bound by it at once: read the target state below, check this project against it, and add your own tasks to comply on your own schedule. Nothing in this project was changed except the appending of this task.

THE TARGET STATE, in the operator's words of 2026-10-12:
  Private networks (VPN) and SSH hosts are provided machine-wide by the operator. A project reaches them only through the host definitions the machine provides. It never starts its own VPN client, never uses passwords or sshpass, never copies SSH or VPN keys between machines, and never disables host-key checking. SSH logins use the keys or certificates the operator provides. VPN and SSH credentials are issued from the operator's KMS-encrypted store into the machine's own configuration; a project never reads, copies or creates them. When a connection fails (expired certificate, unknown or changed host key, VPN down), that item waits for the operator and other work continues. This rule does not bind the repository whose work is providing them.

WHAT TO CHECK in this project's own scripts, documentation and configuration: anything that starts a VPN client; passwords or sshpass used for SSH; SSH or VPN keys copied between machines; host-key checking turned off (StrictHostKeyChecking=no, UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null) or unknown host keys accepted automatically (StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new); a host reached by anything other than the machine's own host definitions; a key, certificate or VPN credential that the project reads, creates or stores.

VERIFY, do not assume. The central repo has not read this project's files for this rule. If none of the above occurs here, that is an answer: record it and close this task. If the rule does not apply to this project at all, mark this task superseded with the reason.
